standard_prerequisites.name: An equality of elements of a ring of the form det(id + a b) = det(id + b a) may be checked after localizing at every prime, and over a local ring a finite projective module is finite free
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 36431-36433, where the author replaces R by a localization at a prime ideal and then assumes R local with M and N finite free
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the statement for arbitrary finite projective modules over an arbitrary ring to the matrix identity of the next step, over a commutative ring of the simplest kind.

standard_prerequisites.name: In characteristic zero the determinant of a square matrix of size at most N is a universal polynomial in the traces of the powers of that matrix
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: invoked at proof lines 36442-36445, where the author passes to the fraction field of the polynomial ring and then uses that a universal polynomial expresses the determinant in the traces of the powers
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the matrix identity for the two rectangular matrices AB and BA into the family of trace identities Trace((I_n + AB)^k) = Trace((I_m + BA)^k), which is what can be expanded.

standard_prerequisites.name: The trace identity Trace(XY) = Trace(YX) for matrices of compatible size, and the factorizations (AB)^k = A(BA)^{k-1}B and (BA)^k = (BA)^{k-1}AB
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the last step: the traces of all powers agree, hence by the previous item the two determinants agree.

core_obligations: Reduce to the local case: note that it suffices to prove the identity after replacing R by the localization at a prime ideal, so that M and N may be assumed finite free, and rewrite the statement as the matrix identity det(I_n + AB) = det(I_m + BA) with A of size n by m and B of size m by n (proof lines 36431-36438).

Reduce to the universal ring: specialize to R = Z[a_ij, b_ji] with independent variables as entries of A and B, so that the identity in this universal case pulls back to every other ring, and then pass to the fraction field, arriving at the case of a field of characteristic zero (proof lines 36438-36443).

Replace determinants by traces: in characteristic zero the determinant of a matrix of size at most N is a universal polynomial in the traces of its powers, so it suffices to prove Trace((I_n + AB)^k) = Trace((I_m + BA)^k) for every k at least 1 (proof lines 36443-36448).

Reduce the binomial expansion of the two traces to the single family Trace((AB)^k) = Trace((BA)^k) for all k at least 0, by expanding (I + X)^k and using that the identity in each fixed degree k is linear in the trace of the k-th power (proof lines 36449-36450).

Prove the remaining trace identities: the case k = 1 is the classical Trace(AB) = Trace(BA), and for k greater than 1 it follows by writing (AB)^k = A(BA)^{k-1}B and (BA)^k = (BA)^{k-1}AB and applying the cyclicity of the trace, which closes the proof (proof lines 36451-36455).
proof_roadmap: Localize at a prime to reduce to R local, hence M and N finite free, and rewrite the assertion as det(I_n + AB) = det(I_m + BA) for rectangular matrices (proof lines 36431-36438).
Specialize to the polynomial ring in the matrix entries and pass to its fraction field, reducing to a field of characteristic zero (proof lines 36438-36443).
Convert the determinant identity into trace identities by the universal polynomial expressing determinants through the traces of powers (proof lines 36443-36448).

Expand the binomial expression to reduce to Trace((AB)^k) = Trace((BA)^k), prove k = 1 as the classical trace identity and deduce the higher cases from the factorizations (AB)^k = A(BA)^{k-1}B and (BA)^k = (BA)^{k-1}AB (proof lines 36449-36455).
difficulty_reason: The statement is Sylvester's determinant identity in the form det(id + a b) = det(id + b a) for two R-linear maps a : M -> N and b : N -> M between finite projective modules over an arbitrary ring R (statement lines 36419-36428). The proof is a three-stage reduction that is not a single routine computation: it first localizes at a prime to make the two modules finite free, then specializes to the universal polynomial ring in the matrix entries and passes to its fraction field so that the identity may be checked over a field of characteristic zero, and finally replaces the determinant by the traces of the powers of the matrix through a universal polynomial, leaving only the classical trace identity Trace((AB)^k) = Trace((BA)^k) (proof lines 36431-36454). The characteristic-zero input is what makes the passage from determinants to traces legitimate, since a determinant of size at most N is a polynomial expression in the traces of the powers there. The whole argument is inside the counted span, which refers to no labelled item of the chapter and cites nothing.
